The binding persists until the caster chooses to forfeit it; if the ghost's permanent Essence was 0 when bound, maintaining the binding after each recurrence costs ten motes per instance, but otherwise it renews automatically. This spell is commonly used by Deathlords and Abyssals to inflict repeated torture on a captive ghost.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 138

name: Shadow Stones Travel
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; temporarily converts a portion of Creation into a shadowland overlay that spreads over three turns, mirroring normal shadowland rules for anyone inside, with the inverse effect if cast within the Underworld.
description: This spell temporarily converts a portion of Creation into a shadowland, with the overlay spreading to a fifty-yard radius over the course of three turns. The transformed area follows normal shadowland rules for anyone caught within it for a number of turns equal to the necromancer's Essence, or until she dismisses the effect early. If cast within the Underworld instead, the spell has the inverse effect, temporarily revealing a patch of Creation.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 138

name: Shield of Shattering Bones
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; lets the caster reflexively shunt incoming damage onto a marked, nearby animate-dead minion in line of sight, which visibly bears the transferred blow.
description: At the time of casting, the necromancer marks a nearby animate-dead minion (such as a skeleton or zombie) within five times her Essence in yards and in line of sight. Thereafter, for a reflexive cost of three motes, she may shunt an incoming attack's damage onto the marked minion instead of suffering it herself; the minion visibly displays the transferred blow, such as a skeleton's ribcage collapsing. The marked minion remains valid until sunrise (within the Underworld) or until the spell is recast to mark a new minion.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 139

name: Silenced Whispered Prayers
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; cuts off a target's incoming worship, dropping a single target's Cult rating to zero for the spell's duration, or halving or reducing all Cult ratings within a wide area if cast on a region instead.
description: Cast on a single target, this spell drops that target's Cult rating (Underworld or Ancestor) to zero for the spell's duration. Cast instead on an area (a forty-five-yard radius), it reduces every ghost's Cult rating within the area by one dot, and halves (rounding down) the Cult rating of living creatures within it. The spell's effect lasts until the Underworld's sun has risen seven times.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 139

name: Sweet Voice Familiar
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; the caster's body goes slack and possessed, broadcasting maddening Whispers of Oblivion to every ghost within miles equal to her Essence, risking a taint effect on ghosts who fail a Willpower roll and draining temporary Willpower from mortals who hear it.
description: The necromancer's body goes slack, possessed by the spell, and broadcasts maddening Whispers of Oblivion to every ghost within a number of miles equal to her Essence. Affected ghosts must beat a Willpower roll at a difficulty equal to the caster's Whispers rating plus five, or become poisoned by the promises of Oblivion (see Exalted: The Abyssals, p. 284 sidebar). Mortals who hear the broadcast must roll Willpower against the caster's Whispers rating, losing temporary Willpower equal to their margin of failure.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 139

name: Incomparable Destruction Engine (aka Obsidian Reanimation)
summary: Void Circle necromancy spell; the most powerful war-machine animation spell, required to bring size class 4 (colossal) war machines such as Juggernaut and the web is the spider to life, with the strongest baseline Attributes/Abilities and most health levels per necrosurgery success of the three animation spells.
description: Also known among necromancers as Obsidian Reanimation, this is the most powerful of the three war-machine animation spells and the only one capable of animating size class 4 (colossal) war machines. No necromancer can even attempt to cast it without Craft (Necrosurgery) •••••, and each necrosurgery roll represents three full days of work. The spell's minimum Essence cost equals the number of successes needed on the necrosurgery roll, which the Storyteller may double for truly colossal machines such as Juggernaut. A war machine animated this way has: Strength 8, Dexterity 3, Stamina 7, Charisma 0, Manipulation 0, Appearance 0, Perception 4, Intelligence 2, Wits 4; no functioning Virtues (automatically succeeds on Valor rolls, automatically fails all others); Athletics 4, Awareness 3, Brawl 6, Dodge 2, Endurance 4, Melee 4, Resistance 5, Stealth 1; Base Initiative 8; and, per success on the initial necrosurgery roll, three -0, three -1 and four -2 health levels.
cost: Minimum Essence equal to the number of successes needed on the animating Craft (Necrosurgery) roll (doubled at Storyteller discretion for colossal machines).
target: one war machine of size class 4 built via the war-machine-construction-framework

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 99

name: Oblivion's Avatar
summary: Void Circle necromancy spell; invests an animated war machine with a portion of the Malfeans' own power, granting it a chosen channel of entropy into Creation -- a black nimbus of destruction akin to Crypt Bolt or Withering Method, a disease-spreading effect, or some other direct conduit for Oblivion.
description: Animating a war machine is sometimes just the first step toward creating a truly devastating weapon. Oblivion's Avatar invests a walking war machine with a portion of the power of the Malfeans themselves, granting it the ability to carry pure entropy into Creation. This might manifest as a black nimbus of destruction akin to the Abyssal Charms Crypt Bolt or (Material) Withering Method, the ability to spread disease, or some other form of direct channeling of Oblivion into the realm of the living; the prayer-blocking ability of the artifact weapon of mephitic desolation is cited as one product of this spell. Casting it costs 10 committed motes per granted power, or 40 motes and 5 experience points per power to make that power permanent.
cost: 10 motes (committed) per power, or 40 motes and 5 experience points per power to make the effect permanent

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 102

name: The Barless Gate
summary: Void Circle mirror spell; grants instant travel between any two mirrors in the Underworld, shattering any wards at the recipient mirror's location.
description: This Void Circle mirror spell allows instantaneous travel between any two mirrors in the Underworld, and its passage shatters any wards protecting the location of the recipient mirror.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 120

name: Folding Midnight
summary: Void Circle version of Midnight Shadow Sun; permanently curses a shadowland border to function as a one-way portal in a single direction, requiring the necromancer to walk its perimeter at the proper time of day.
description: This greater, Void Circle version of Midnight Shadow Sun permanently curses a shadowland's border to become a one-way portal that only permits crossing in a single direction. Casting it requires the necromancer to walk the entire perimeter of the shadowland at the time of day appropriate to her desired effect; an unlucky ghost or other creature caught by it may find itself permanently unable to return to the side it started from.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 128

name: Empty Night Future
summary: Void Circle version of Silent Master's Pollen; frees up to ten ghosts within a ten-yard radius from any binding effect regardless of Essence, risking Oblivion instead of Lethe on a failed Willpower roll.
description: This greatest, Void Circle version of Silent Master's Pollen affects up to ten ghosts within a ten-yard radius simultaneously and frees them from any binding effect regardless of its Essence rating. Each struck ghost must beat a Willpower roll at difficulty 5 or be drawn into Oblivion instead of Lethe; the necromancer absorbs one mote of agony for each soul lost this way.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 130

name: Blackstorm Wagon
summary: Void Circle version of Clamoring Shackles; a single accuracy roll applies a rain of magical arrows to every target in a hundred-yard radius within five hundred yards, with any ghost slain suffering the same grave-chain fate.
description: This greater, Void Circle version of Clamoring Shackles rains down a barrage of magical arrows: the necromancer makes a single Perception + Archery roll that applies to every target within a hundred-yard radius, out to a range of five hundred yards. Any ghost slain by one of these arrows suffers the same soulsteel grave-prison chain fate as a target of Clamoring Shackles.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 132

name: Void Cocoon Warrior
summary: Void Circle variant of Rattled Bones of War; a black cocoon of nothingness becomes a twenty-foot noble or royal warstrider that can be upgraded with a lethal health level sacrifice, lasting two hours and extendable at additional cost.
description: This greater, Void Circle variant of Rattled Bones of War forms a black cocoon of nothingness around the necromancer that becomes a twenty-foot mighty noble or royal warstrider. The necromancer may sacrifice a lethal health level to upgrade the construct to a ruddy-red royal warstrider that cannot be healed until the spell ends. It lasts two hours, extendable by paying motes equal to half the spell's original cost per additional hour, and can mount additional Void Cocoon weapons at an extra Essence-based cost.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 137

name: Birth of Sanity's Sorrow
summary: Void Circle spell, castable only once per lifetime in the instant before death and taught directly by a Malfean; transforms the caster into a unique hungry-ghost-like combat form for one scene before she irrevocably dies, her soul devoured by the Void.
description: This spell can only be cast once per lifetime, and only in the instant before the necromancer's death, having been taught to her directly by a Malfean. It transforms her into a unique hungry-ghost-like combat form, using the hungry ghost rules (see Exalted: The Abyssals, pp. 61-62) with her Essence added to her Strength and Stamina, and a number of health levels equal to five times her Essence plus an Incapacitated level. Charms cost only one mote each to invoke in this form, and a single mote can substitute for a point of Willpower. The form comes with three unique, bespoke powers costing five to ten motes each, devised jointly by the Storyteller and player. The form remains active for one scene, after which the necromancer instantly and irrevocably dies, her soul devoured by the Void — unless she was already Incapacitated at the moment of casting, in which case she instead survives at the Incapacitated health level. [NOTE: this is a capstone, character-ending transformation spell rather than a standard combat spell, and its bespoke powers are explicitly GM/player-collaborative content rather than fixed mechanics.]

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 139

name: Black Faith
summary: Void Circle desperate-suicide ritual; the caster sacrifices a ghost to the Abyss after a half-hour of worship, then leaps into the Void, either being teleported anywhere by the pleased Malfeans or destroyed permanently if they are unimpressed.
description: In this desperate ritual, the necromancer sacrifices a ghost's pain and corpus to the Abyss after a half-hour of dedicated worship, then leaps bodily into the Void. If the Malfeans are pleased with the offering, they revoke her intended dissolution and instead teleport her anywhere she wishes — the Labyrinth, the Underworld, or Creation — bypassing all wards along the way. If they are unimpressed, she is instead destroyed, permanently and without recourse. This spell's outcome is explicitly Storyteller-adjudicated and should be used in close coordination with the Storyteller.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 140

name: Forsaken Life Engine
summary: Void Circle spell; conjures a yeddim-sized bone-and-iron engine that devours fed living creatures to permanently carve out a shadowland centered on itself, complete with its own combat statistics and mounted weapons.
description: The necromancer conjures a vast engine of bone and iron, roughly the size of a yeddim, that devours living creatures fed into it. Once creatures with a cumulative permanent Essence of at least ten times the motes spent have been consumed, the engine carves out a permanent shadowland with a fifty-mile radius (extendable by another fifty miles per additional ten motes spent) centered on itself. The engine has Strength 6, Dexterity 4, Stamina 6, Perception 2, Intelligence 2, Wits 4, a relevant combat Ability of 3, soaks of 22L/30B, and sixty health levels; damage must exceed its soak to harm it at all, Obsidian Countermagic destroys it instantly, and Adamant Countermagic deals ten health levels of damage to it. It can process up to five creatures per minute (one every four turns) and self-destructs in a fiery explosion with a five-hundred-yard blast radius if destroyed. Its weapons are Engine Claws (Speed -2, Accuracy +3, Damage +6L, Defense +0), Fragment (Accuracy +0, Damage +7L, Rate 3, Range 100), and Blood (Accuracy +3, Damage +6L, Rate 1, Range 25).

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 140

name: The Clay of Warped Dreams
summary: Void Circle spell; requires sacrificing three ghosts after a ten-minute prayer to the Malfeans while standing in the Labyrinth, granting total reshaping control over ten square miles of the Labyrinth for as long as Essence remains committed.
description: Standing within the Labyrinth, the necromancer offers a ten-minute prayer to the Malfeans and sacrifices three ghosts, destroying them, to grant herself total control over ten square miles of the Labyrinth, reshaping it to her will. While the spell is committed, she can manifest physical attacks (using Wits plus the appropriate combat Ability plus Occult successes) or create hazards and creatures at the Storyteller's discretion. Control lasts as long as the Essence remains committed, or until a dead god reclaims the reshaped space.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 140

name: Mouth of the Void
summary: Void Circle mass-death spell; the caster's mouth yawns open, pouring out a spreading darkness that devours every living creature within a forty-yard radius, dealing thirty levels of aggravated damage and leaving the ground pitted with obsidian.
description: The necromancer intones dark words, and cold shadows flare about her mouth like the lashing tails of a hundred preying cats. As she speaks, her mouth yawns wide and darkness pours out, rippling outward like an oil slick to fill a forty-yard radius over the course of the casting. As the spell ends, the darkness stills before falling into the sky like a silent reverse waterfall, blotting out all light within its boundary as it does. To anyone caught within, the blackness feels alive, clawing, grasping, whispering, and nibbling, removing parts of their innermost flesh and being. After the shadow takes these things, it leaves them, departing for the Void and the end of all life: each living creature within its reach suffers thirty levels of aggravated damage. The earth beneath the devouring shadow is left rotting and pitted, strewn with large chunks of obsidian — the transformed remains of any creature the spell killed.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 141

name: Pyre-Flame Guardian
summary: Void Circle spell; the necromancer doubles in height and fuses soulsteel skin from a dozen sacrificed ghosts to become a devastating melee combatant wreathed in unquenchable green pyre flame, exploding violently when the spell ends.
description: As the casting completes, a dozen random ghosts are torn, shrieking, into Oblivion, and their anguish crawls onto the necromancer's skin, fusing into soulsteel that coats her entire body while she grows to twice her normal height. The soulsteel armor grants +12L/+12B soak and ignores any attack dealing fewer than twelve dice of raw damage. Her Strength gains a bonus equal to her Essence, and a billowing sheath of pyre flame inflicts three dice of aggravated damage upon any who dare attack her barehanded vision of harrowing death; anyone attacking with weapons not forged of stone or one of the Five Magical Materials sees their weapon slowly consumed and burned away in their hands. She can also hurl balls of pyre flame as a dice action using Thrown + Dexterity, dealing three health levels of aggravated damage plus one die per extra success, unparryable without Charms; where these flames strike, they leave circles and streaks of green fire across the scenery, and any barehanded attack that connects inflicts three more levels of aggravated damage and blows green fire blossoms across the land. Victims of the guardian's pyre flame must scrape it off (two levels of lethal damage per turn spent doing so, taking three turns) or continue burning; only creatures armored in a Magical Material, in stone, or in armor made entirely of one, are immune to the flame's spread. The spell ends when the caster cancels it, when an hour has passed (per the Calendar of Setesh), or when struck by Obsidian Countermagic; however it ends, the necromancer's soulsteel skin explodes into a thousand screaming shards traced in green fire, dealing five levels of lethal and two of aggravated damage to everyone within thirty yards, avoidable only with a perfect defense. The pyre flame this spell creates behaves as ordinary pyre flame in all respects (see Exalted: The Abyssals, p. 256): sunlight in Creation extinguishes it within minutes, in shadowlands it burns out within a year unless refreshed by sunlight, and in the Underworld it is permanent. Weapon table: Pyre-Flame Ball (Accuracy +Essence, Damage +3A, Rate 5, Range 30).

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 141

name: Grandmother Void
summary: Void Circle spell; the caster becomes a flat, empty silhouette — a living doorway into Oblivion — that spawns fully material spectres each turn to obey her commands in the Malfeans' name, at the risk of a taint roll for anyone who hears their whispers.
description: Speaking two words of the Old Realm tongue, the necromancer becomes a flat, empty silhouette — a doorway into Oblivion — for a number of turns equal to her Essence. Each turn, two spectres spawn fully formed from her, complete with full Essence and health levels, created using the starting ghost rules plus bonus experience equal to seven times the necromancer's Essence, with stats set by the necromancer herself. These spectres obey the necromancer's commands in the name of the Malfeans. Hearing their whispers risks a Willpower + Essence roll at difficulty 5 to avoid Oblivion's taint (see Exalted: The Abyssals, p. 284). While the caster is filled with infinite nothingness in this form, she is immune to physical and mental assaults; Obsidian or Adamant Countermagic cast during this period returns her to herself and ends the spell early, but will not dispel any spectres she has already brought forth.

sources.bookLabel: The Book of Bone and Ebony

sourceDisplay: The Book of Bone and Ebony, p. 142

name: Risen and Screaming
summary: Void Circle spell; sows an area with latent undeath by walking a looped boundary, so that any living creature that later dies inside the loop rises minutes afterward as a fast, screaming zombie bound to that ground.
description: Focusing dark energy inward, the necromancer walks a looped path around a stretch of fertile earth in Creation; the soil beneath her feet blackens and dries as if charred and salted as she walks. Once she completes the loop there are no immediately apparent effects, but the enclosed land has been sown with lasting undeath. Triggered by the sudden rush of spirit that accompanies any death, when a living creature breathes its last breath and falls within the boundary, the ground crumbles beneath it; the creature sinks into the dirt and rises minutes later as an animate, rotting zombie. The zombies created by this spell are under the necromancer's control if she is present; otherwise they remain stationary unless a living creature becomes visible, at which point they attempt to slay it, propagating the undeath. These zombies cannot leave the circle that birthed them — they will not try, and instantly become inanimate if forced outside the boundary. They scream loudly when they spot prey and move at twice the speed of normal zombies; lacking victims, they bury themselves in the welcoming earth (noticeable only via a Perception + Awareness roll at difficulty two), remaining perfectly aware of all creatures within ten yards and able to claw free as a turn's movement. Otherwise, they are identical to the zombies described in Exalted (p. 299) and are always extras. The enclosed area returns to normal one week per point of the necromancer's Essence after the boundary was walked, though the ground itself will never bear life again.

name: Summon Hekatonkhire
summary: Void Circle six-hour ritual requiring the death of a mortal and a ghost (or one Ghost-Blooded); summons a monstrous hekatonkhire — a reforged fragment of a dead Primordial's soul — and forces a contested soul-duel to determine whether it serves the necromancer or destroys her.
description: This six-hour ritual requires the death of both a mortal and a ghost (or a single Ghost-Blooded, see the Exalted Players Guide) as part of the casting, and ends at dusk. Once complete, it calls forth one of the great and fearsome hekatonkhire — dead-god remnants formed from the souls of things that fell in flesh alongside the Primordials during the Primordial War, myriad in shape and form. The necromancer and the summoned hekatonkhire engage in a contested Willpower + Essence duel; the necromancer may spend Essence in seven-mote increments to reduce the creature's dice pool by one die per expenditure. Rolls continue each turn until either side accumulates three more successes than the other. If the necromancer wins, the hekatonkhire serves her loyally for a year and a day, or she may set it to a single indefinite task instead; if the hekatonkhire wins, it consumes the summoner's body and soul and returns to the Underworld. [NOTE: this spell summons a Storyteller-controlled monster type; a sample hekatonkhire NPC ("Loras, Death Sun") is provided on the following page but is GM-facing content and is not reproduced in this inventory. The casting and soul-duel mechanics above are player-facing and are what this row tracks.]

name: Sins of the Father
summary: Void Circle spell; curses a living victim with eternal servitude via a never-healing facial scar that passes to all their descendants, guaranteeing that when the marked person dies they become a ghost bound to obey the caster's every command.
description: The necromancer lays a curse of eternal servitude upon a living victim, marking her with a scar — most commonly on the face — that never heals despite any mundane or magical treatment, and which appears identically on all of the victim's descendants while she lives. The victim can be marked in person, by lightly brushing her with the caster's fingers at the climax of the casting, or remotely through an arcane link, which is destroyed in the process. The curse inflicts no other miseries while the marked creature lives, but when she dies, she automatically becomes a ghost possessing the Passion "Obey She Who Cursed Me" at a rating equal to her new Conviction, and must immediately seek out and forever obey every command of her master. Even the caster's own death does not free the cursed line: they instead become bound to the necromancer's next incarnation, although they are free to take retribution against the original caster's reincarnation, should she rise again as a ghost herself. Obsidian Countermagic can free a single cursed individual (without freeing any relatives), while Adamant Countermagic frees a victim permanently but kills her in the process. Only a Zenith Caste priest assisted by a Solar Circle sorcerer, petitioning the Unconquered Sun, can free a victim without killing her or resorting to comparably dark magic. The Celestial Exalted cannot be enslaved by this spell, though they can still be marked and pass the curse to their children. Creatures without souls, or whose souls never enter the Underworld, are entirely immune.

name: Iron Countermagic
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; either shields the caster from hostile Shadowlands Circle necromancy for a turn, or actively extinguishes a single such spell at range, with stronger Onyx/Obsidian tiers unlocked by Labyrinth/Void Circle Necromancy.
description: With this spell, the Exalted can absorb and smother the energy of hostile necromancy. If the character spends 10 motes, she may slash at the air, tearing ribbons of black power to swirl and bleed around her person. This shield negates all hostile spells of the Shadowlands Circle directed at her until the end of the next turn, but its cold seeps into her joints and bones, inflicting a -2 penalty to all Physical actions for as long as it persists. Alternately, for 20 motes, the caster can extinguish a single Shadowlands Circle spell within a number of feet equaling her permanent Essence x 50. Extant spells are disintegrated, while spells in the process of being cast are torn asunder. This spell is extremely fast and takes effect as soon as the character spends Willpower. Countermagic can banish summoned ghosts, although it cannot break bonds of servitude wrought by necromancy. Spells countered with Iron Countermagic shatter without inflicting any side effects; if used to counter a lower circle, the countermagic utterly annihilates the spell with no side effects or collateral damage. Countered Void Circle spells still mar bystanders and ravage the earth, although in most cases the backlash pales compared to the intended effects. More powerful versions of this spell exist at higher circles: Onyx for Labyrinth, Obsidian for Void. Each protects against spells of its own circle or below. Necromantic countermagic can also oppose sorcery if it is one circle or higher, and vice versa; thus Sapphire Countermagic (Exalted, p. 221) may counter Shadowlands Circle spells, while Obsidian Countermagic may block Celestial Circle Sorcery. The personal shield/direct-extinguishing costs for Onyx and Obsidian are 15 motes/20 motes and 20 motes/25 motes respectively.
cost: 10 or 20 motes (Onyx and Obsidian tiers cost more; see description)
duration: Until the end of the next turn (shield) or Instant (extinguish)
target: Caster (shield) or one spell effect within range (extinguish)

name: Brick-by-Brick Solitude
summary: Labyrinth Circle upgrade of Ringing Hun Rebuke; the resonating rings keep ghosts at a full radius scaling with Essence and unable to make hand-to-hand attacks.
description: This is the greater Labyrinth Circle version of Ringing Hun Rebuke. When cast, several dozen arcane symbols appear in a cylinder around the necromancer. Bright, as if drawn with pure sunlight, they expand rapidly to a radius equal to the caster's permanent Essence x 10 yards. Any ghosts closer than that boundary are pushed out to it as the wall expands. Ghosts are unable to pierce this boundary and, therefore, cannot make hand-to-hand attacks; ranged attacks suffer a loss of half their successes before they reach the necromancer. Brick-by-Brick Solitude does not increase the caster's Strength: while the boundary moves with him and will shove most ghosts out of his path with little effort, a sufficiently determined mob can still resist being pushed past a number of ghosts equal to three times his Strength rating. The source text does not restate a separate mote cost or duration for this greater version; it is presented purely as a variant description following Ringing Hun Rebuke's own entry.

name: Barred Tomb
summary: Void Circle version of Denying the Call; extends the temporary revival to up to an hour with health levels equal to the caster's Essence, and binds the revived creature to obey the necromancer's will for the duration.
description: There exists a Void Circle variation of Denying the Call, called Barred Tomb, which places a recently departed soul back into its body for up to an hour, with a number of health levels equal to the caster's Essence, binding it to obey the necromancer's will for the duration. Like Denying the Call, these health levels can only be lost to aggravated damage, and this spell cannot be cast upon a target who has already been affected by Denying the Call or by Barred Tomb. Once a spirit is released by Barred Tomb, it appears in the Underworld with only a single health level.
